title: Canonical Examples (Streaming + Tools + Structured Output) — Outline Draft
content:
Working doc / rough narrative outline for the canonical examples refresh. This is not the “spec” (that lives in Confluence). Purpose here: nail the story and what we show/do NOT show in user-facing examples across Python/TS/Go + docs-site pages.

Owner: Sabrina (examples/polish)
Tech lead: Ibrahim (event model / parity)
Docs program: Elliot / Wei
PM: Henry
Security review: Marcus

----

0) Goals for the examples (what we’re optimizing for)
- Copy/paste runnable with minimal setup (API key env var + install + run)
- Consistent conceptual flow across Python/TypeScript/Go:
  - How to read streaming events
  - How to handle tool call deltas safely
  - How to request structured output + validate + retry
- Reduce top support pain:
  - “Stream disconnected mid-response”
  - “Tool args are partial / invalid JSON”
  - “Schema mismatch / silent parse failures”
- Avoid insecure patterns:
  - No “execute shell command” examples
  - No arbitrary network calls to user-provided URLs
  - Always show tool allowlist + argument validation

Non-goals:
- We are not redesigning SDK APIs.
- We are not documenting every event type; just the ones needed for typical product integrations.

----

1) Proposed docs & examples information architecture (narrative flow)

1.1 Landing / intro block (short)
- “These examples show production-safe patterns for streaming, tool calling, and structured output.”
- “Same flow in Python/TypeScript/Go; pick your language.”
- “If you’re upgrading from legacy ‘functions’ docs, see terminology note.”

1.2 Example 1 — Token streaming (baseline)
- Teach the streaming loop first, BEFORE tools and schemas.
- Show:
  - Setting a request timeout
  - Iterating events / handling token deltas
  - Collecting final response object (users keep missing “final”)
  - Handling disconnects gracefully (surface actionable error)

1.3 Example 2 — Tool calling (single tool)
- Introduce tool definitions + allowlist.
- Demonstrate incremental tool-call-arguments accumulation (deltas).
- Validate tool args before executing.
- Return tool result back to model.

1.4 Example 3 — Tool calling (parallel tools)
- Show parallel tool invocations with concurrency control.
- Make it explicit: tool calls can arrive interleaved in the stream; arguments may be partial until completion.
- Show a safe pattern for joining results and continuing the model.

1.5 Example 4 — Structured output (schema-based)
- Show:
  - “Here is a JSON Schema (versioned)”
  - Request structured output
  - Validate response
  - Retry strategy on parse/validation failure
  - Fallback/escape hatch guidance (“if strict schema is too brittle, choose a looser schema or a two-pass approach”)

1.6 Troubleshooting appendix (small but concrete)
- Streaming:
  - Proxy buffering (corporate proxies, load balancers)
  - Idle timeouts / long generation
  - Resume/retry guidance (where SDK supports it)
- Tools:
  - Partial args are expected mid-stream
  - “Do not JSON.parse until tool call is complete”
  - Duplicate tool call ids / out-of-order deltas (rare; what to do)
- Structured output:
  - Schema mismatch error messages (what they mean)
  - Version pinning and upgrade strategy

----

2) Terminology + naming conventions (proposed)

2.1 Tools vs functions
- User-facing term: “tool calling”
- Accept “function calling” as legacy synonym but prefer “tools” everywhere.
- In code:
  - Use variable names: tools, toolResult, toolCall
  - Avoid “function” in new snippets unless SDK API forces it.

2.2 Structured output naming
- User-facing: “Structured output” (schema-based)
- Avoid “JSON mode” unless specifically referencing legacy behavior.
- Use “JSON Schema” explicitly.

2.3 Streaming event naming (canonical)
NOTE: This is narrative guidance (the actual event taxonomy is in the canonical patterns Confluence page).
- Use “event” as the generic term.
- Prefer these labels in prose and comments:
  - token delta (text delta)
  - tool call delta (args delta)
  - final response
- Always show the “final response” capture pattern.

2.4 IDs and aggregation keys
- Tool calls must be aggregated by tool_call_id (or equivalent field) NOT by tool name.
- For parallel tools: multiple active tool calls at once.

2.5 Error language (what we say)
- Avoid blame-y wording.
- Make errors actionable:
  - “Tool arguments are incomplete; wait for completion event before parsing.”
  - “Schema validation failed at path …; retrying with tightened instructions.”

----

3) Canonical example set: content outline + constraints per example

3.1 Example: Streaming tokens (no tools)
Audience: first-time users; also used by support to debug “why did my stream stop?”
Minimum code requirements:
- Show environment variable usage (REDWOOD_API_KEY)
- Show request with streaming enabled
- Event loop skeleton with:
  - token delta handling
  - error handling with timeout
  - final aggregation

Edge cases to mention (in comments or short callout):
- Disconnect mid-stream: tell user to retry (idempotency note if we have it), and set timeouts correctly.
- Proxy buffering: recommend disabling buffering / increasing read timeout.

What NOT to include:
- No custom reconnect/resume logic unless the SDK supports it cleanly.
- No deep SSE explanations.

3.2 Example: Tool calling (single tool)
Tool choice (keep harmless):
- “lookup_order_status(order_id)” with a tiny in-memory map
- or “get_weather(city)” but DO NOT call the internet; mock data only

Requirements:
- Tool allowlist
- Arg validation (basic: required fields, type checks)
- Safe JSON parse strategy:
  - accumulate string deltas
  - parse only when we have the complete tool arguments payload
- Clear loop:
  1) Model requests tool
  2) We execute tool
  3) We send tool result
  4) Model returns final answer

Open question: do we include a “tool args incomplete” branch in the mainline code or just in troubleshooting?
- My suggestion: include minimal guard (don’t parse until complete) in-line; keep the heavy explanation in troubleshooting.

3.3 Example: Tool calling (parallel tools)
Goal: make the interleaving + concurrency story unambiguous.

Proposed scenario:
- “extract_entities(text)” and “lookup_customer(customer_id)” OR
- “fetch_pricing(sku)” and “check_inventory(sku)” (both local mocks)

Requirements:
- Concurrency control (do not spawn unbounded goroutines/promises/threads)
- Deterministic ordering for tool results submission (or explain it’s not required)
- Aggregation by tool_call_id

Edge cases to mention:
- Interleaved deltas for multiple tool calls
- Partial JSON per tool call is expected

What NOT to include:
- No “fire off tools based on user input without allowlist.”
- No demonstration of tools with side effects.

3.4 Example: Structured output (JSON Schema)
Goal: the most copy/paste and “works in prod” snippet we can provide.

Requirements:
- Provide schema inline (but also show how to version it)
- Parse + validate:
  - Python: jsonschema or pydantic? (need consistency w/ SDK owners)
  - TS: zod + schema mapping
  - Go: encoding/json + validation helper (or gojsonschema)
- Retry strategy:
  - Attempt 1: strict schema + “return valid JSON only” instruction
  - On validation error:
    - log redacted error
    - retry with explicit callout of the failure (“Your previous output failed because …”) and restate constraints
  - Cap retries (2 total attempts recommended)
- Failure mode:
  - If still invalid, return a typed error; show how to surface it.

Open questions:
- Should we standardize on JSON Schema draft version in examples? (Draft 2020-12 vs 07)
  - Need alignment w/ API standards doc + what gateway enforces.
- Should we include a “lenient” mode example?
  - Current inclination: keep main example strict; include a short “If you need robustness…” note suggesting a looser schema or two-pass extraction.

----

4) Cross-SDK parity notes (what we must keep identical)

4.1 Conceptual parity checklist
- Same section headings & narrative steps across languages.
- Same tool names + schemas across languages (only syntax changes).
- Same retry policy language.
- Same troubleshooting callouts.

4.2 SDK-specific deviations (allowed, but must be documented)
- Idiomatic cancellation:
  - TS: AbortController
  - Go: context.Context deadline
  - Python: timeout args / context manager (depending on SDK)
- Streaming iteration differences (iterator vs callback/event emitter)

Rule: if an SDK forces different code structure, the comments must map back to the canonical steps.

----

5) Edge cases: include vs exclude (explicit)

Include (must cover somewhere)
- Partial tool args / tool-call deltas are normal
- Stream disconnect handling (timeouts, proxy buffering)
- Validation failures for structured output + retry pattern
- Safe logging / redaction

Exclude (do not teach in canonical examples)
- Autonomously deciding to call tools based on model output without allowlist
- Tools that run shell commands, access the filesystem, or fetch arbitrary URLs
- “Just regex the JSON out” parsing hacks
- Unlimited retries / silent fallback to unvalidated output

----

6) Style + editorial rules for snippets
- Keep snippets < ~120 lines if possible; move helper utilities to a small “helpers” section.
- Always show dependencies explicitly:
  - pip install … / npm install … / go get …
- Always show where to set REDWOOD_API_KEY.
- Avoid placeholder pseudo-code where possible; runnable > clever.
- Comment style:
  - Use short, direct comments (“Accumulate tool args deltas by tool_call_id.”)
  - Don’t narrate obvious syntax.

----

7) Verification plan (how we ensure these don’t drift)
- Canonical examples live in redwood-examples repo.
- Docs-site and SDK READMEs should link to canonical snippets and/or import from them where possible.
- Snippet tests:
  - Lint + run against mock server as default
  - Optional staging run behind a manual/cron workflow with rate-limit safe settings

Open question: should docs code blocks be generated from redwood-examples (single source of truth) or copied?
- Leaning: generated/embedded where tooling allows; otherwise copy with snippet tests verifying text blocks.

----

8) Open questions / TODOs (tracked)
- Decide final user-facing terminology: “Tools” vs “Functions” (PM-612)
- Confirm final streaming event semantics language with API team (ENG-2848)
- Confirm schema draft/version guidance in standards doc is stable enough for examples
- Decide which validation libraries to standardize on (per language)
- Decide if we include “stream reconnect” snippet or keep it troubleshooting-only

----

9) Notes from prior discussions (quick memory)
- Support tickets show users frequently JSON.parse mid-stream and crash on partial tool args.
- We should explicitly show that final response is separate from deltas and must be captured.
- Security wants the tool examples to be “boring” and obviously safe; emphasize allowlist + validation.

End of doc.
